items.what: The failure message for an unreadable default CSV must contain the literal path 'styles/fixtures/default_names.csv' on stderr
The failure message for a missing translation CSV must contain the literal path 'styles/locale/cs/names.csv' on stderr
The failure message for a missing 'slug' column must contain the literal column name 'slug' on stderr
The failure message for a missing language column must contain the literal 'name_cs' (the concrete name_<lang_code> expansion) on stderr
The warning for an unknown translation slug must mention the offending slug value (e.g. 'unknown-slug') in stderr output
items.quote: grep -q 'unknown-slug' err || fail "F1 missing unknown-slug warning: $(cat err)"

reason: The instruction requires failure and warning logging but never states what the messages must contain; the hidden tests grep stderr for the exact file paths, the column names 'slug'/'name_cs', and the offending slug value. All of those substrings are either stated verbatim in the instruction or mechanical expansions, so a natural error/warning message that names the file, column, or slug passes.
